articles.title: Las Vegas Grand Prix: Formula One 2026 race updates – live
articles.summary: Updates from the Formula 1 GP in Las Vegas. Race gets under way at 8pm local/4am GMT/3pm AEDT. Any thoughts? Get in touch with an email. F1 has taken us to the city of cars, casinos and Elvis weddings this week - the third last race for the year.
body: There’s just 17 points between Max Verstappen in second and George Russell in third, who is just one point ahead of Lewis Hamilton in fourth. It’s anyone’s game.
In fifth is Charles Leclerc who is just three points ahead of Lando Norris - and between the McLaren driver and Verstappen is 33 points.
That means heartbreak for those – including yours truly – who wanted to see a victorious Oscar Piastri. It’s been a disappointing season.

Some of the heat has obviously been taken out of the weekend with both the championship and constructors titles won earlier this month by Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes respectively (as well as the cool temperature on the track).

articles.title: Lionel Messi at center of red-card controversy as Inter Miami face early MLS playoff exit
articles.summary: Messi booked for throwing ball into opponent’s face. Columbus coach insists Argentine deserved red card. Defending champions thrashed 3-0 in series opener. Columbus Crew coach Laurent Courtois said Lionel Messi should have been sent off after throwing a ball into an opponent’s face as Inter Miami…
body: Messi’s frustration boiled over on the stroke of half-time when he hurled a throw-in into the face of Columbus forward Gonzalo Tapia, with 10-man Miami trailing 1-0 at the time.
Messi and Tapia were both shown yellow cards for the incident by referee Allen Chapman, but Courtois said afterwards that the Argentina superstar should have been given a red card.
“Everybody knows that he deserved more than a yellow card,” Courtois said at a post-game press conference when asked about the incident. “It’s just really sad.”
Chapman later defended his decision to show Messi only a yellow card.

articles.title: France beat Argentina to set up Nations Championship final with South Africa
articles.summary: England face All Blacks rematch in third-place game. Ireland take on Australia to decide fifth spot. France and South Africa will contest the inaugural Nations Championship grand final next Sunday in London, while England will face an immediate rematch with the All Blacks next Saturday.
body: Les Bleus defeated Argentina 45-17 in Paris, ultimately overwhelming the Pumas with five second-half tries and seven overall at the Stade de France. They confirmed top spot in the northern hemisphere table with the required bonus-point win, finishing on 26 points with five wins out of six. England (five bonus points) and Ireland (four bonus points) also won five matches, but finish second and third respectively.

The Springboks were earlier defeated 20-17 by Ireland in Dublin, but securing a losing bonus point allowed the world champions to draw level on 22 points with New Zealand, and finish top of the southern hemisphere table with a vastly superior points difference, +135 to +41. South Africa and New Zealand both won four matches in six rounds.

In Cardiff, at the same time as France’s win, Australia ended a four-match losing streak with a 29-26 success against Wales, clinching third place in the southern hemisphere table and setting up a finals weekend clash against Ireland next Friday.

articles.title: MVG still a force to be reckoned with ahead of Grand Slam semi-finals
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen has shown he is still a force to be reckoned with as he prepares to face fellow Dutchman Gian van Veen in his first major semi-final in over a year.
body: With Luke Littler and Luke Humphries already at home, Van Gerwen will be looking to get his hands on some TV silverware for the first time since the 2025 World Series of Darts Finals.

Van Gerwen, who threw perfection in the opening leg agains t Tom Sykes to record his first televised nine-darter on Sky Sports in 14 years, takes on Van Veen on Sunday, with debutant Kevin Doets going head-to-head with three-time champion Gerwyn Price in the first semi-final.

"There has been a lot of criticism about me in the last couple of years, and rightly so, because I wasn't performing. Then you need to make sure you pull your finger out," said Van Gerwen, who traded nine-darters with Sykes on a historic night in Wolverhampton.
"To reach the semi-final is nice, but then to also do it the way I did it today.

articles.title: Southlake Carroll downs Westlake for 2nd straight Class 6A DII state volleyball title
articles.summary: GARLAND - It was deja vu all over again for Central Texas as Southlake Carroll won its second straight UIL Class 6A Division II state championship Saturday at an Austin-area team's expense.
body: Soutlake Carroll (28-11) started this season 10-11 - "We struggled a little bit early in the season," Dragons coach Leslie Jackson said - but then won its next 18 straight matches, including a dominant postseason; the Dragons had lost only one set throughout the playoffs before Westlake took Saturday's third set. The Chaps (41-10) were seeking their fifth title in nine state championship appearances.

Vanessa Glenn, Southlake Carroll's All-American outside hitter who will play for Temple, led the Dragons with 22 kills. Geralynn Byers-Veals had 10 kills for Westlake, which also got nine each from Annabel McDuffee, Caroline Erhlich and Taylor Chorazy. Sunny McWilliams had 14 digs, Clayton Kelly had 12 and Kyrsken Cook (18) and Ellie Ogden (16) combined for 34 assists.

Westlake actually finished with a better hitting percentage (.184 to.153), but Carroll had 30 more attempts and 13 more kills as Westlake's inability to pass to generate adequate offense proved to be the difference in the match.
"I am really proud of the girls," Westlake coach Miguel Saenz said. "They had a tremendous season and played hard to the last point."

articles.title: Alcaraz to face Zverev in ATP Finals title decider
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz will face world number one Alexander Zverev for the ATP Finals title after completing a superb comeback victory against Ben Shelton.
body: The indomitable Spaniard recovered from a flat start to outlast Shelton 3-6 6-3 7-6 (7-1) and secure a return to the showpiece, 12 months after losing to Jannik Sinner.
Alcaraz again competed with strapping around his upper-left leg having injured his hamstring earlier this week, but produced his best tennis when it mattered most.
The seven-time major winner, on a 13-match winning streak, will face Zverev in Sunday's final after the German beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (7-0) 6-4.
Asked how he was feeling physically, with little over 24 hours to recover for that match, Alcaraz said: "Today was a really important test. I think it went great.

On the boys side, Phillips Exeter junior Bocelli Howland-Vlahakis won the Northeast championship in 15:09.6.

articles.title: De Zerbi compares Williams-Barnett to Lamine Yamal - who is Spurs teen?
articles.summary: Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi was not surprised by a dazzling full-debut display from “special” talent Luca Williams-Barnett and compared the 18-year-old to Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal after Saturday’s 2-0 win over Ipswich.
body: De Zerbi turned to the highly rated Spurs academy graduate after two bright cameos and he delivered, scoring on his first Premier League start after 15 minutes before a mazy run set up Dominic Solanke at the start of the second half.

After Williams-Barnett made his senior debut at the age of 16 last season, the clamour for the teenager to play has only increased during a difficult last 12 months, and De Zerbi decided 10 days ago to include him in the starting line-up against Ipswich.

During a chat on Thursday with the skilful England U19 international, De Zerbi asked Williams-Barnett to play with freedom and work hard without the ball "like Raphinha, like [Lamine] Yamal" before he agreed when asked if the teenager could reach similar heights.
After De Zerbi revealed Williams-Barnett prepared for the match on the team bus by watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar, he said: "Luca is a special player.

articles.title: No. 7 North Dakota pulls away in final frames to secure weekend sweep over St. Cloud State
articles.summary: ST. CLOUD — St. Cloud State men’s hockey was able to battle tightly with No. 7 North Dakota, ultimately falling in the third period on both nights. On Friday, the Huskies lost the series opener, 5-3 as freshman forward Carson Pilgrim netted two goals in the contest for his first career multi-goal…
body: The Huskies had the first two power play chances of the game but failed to convert as North Dakota broke through at the end of the first period before Pilgrim found the net for the first time.

North Dakota regained the lead off a ricocheted puck that rebounded off sophomore goaltender Yan Shostak before hitting the top of the net and finding the end of Will Zeller’s stick. Pilgrim once again evened the tally for the Huskies, this time in the waning seconds of the second period to go into the final frame knotted up at two goals each.

After exchanging overturned goals in the first minute, the Fighting Hawks pulled away with two goals in under 90 seconds to take a 4-2 advantage midway through the third period. Junior forward Gavyn Thoreson pulled the Huskies closer with under four minutes to play, but an empty netter would put a bow on the first night in Grand Forks.
The Huskies held a 24-23 edge in shots on goal and played some of their best stretches of hockey thus far this season but fell just short — that’s just hockey.
